what: physics resolve() reported the collision side inverted, so grounded was never true and jump silently did nothing — cost a long time to find because nothing errored
fix: a test that asserts grounded after landing

what: no single call site for hooks; adding behaviours meant finding all four by grep and I still missed one
AGENTS.md listed 'on' as a contribution point; it is not one
no verb attaches a behaviour from a test without saving the level

note: swapped the labels in resolve(); jump had never worked. jump.js now asserts grounded after landing
world.hook(entity, name, ...args) — behaviours then type, one try/catch
AGENTS.md now says the seven points and that on is not one
test.attach / test.detach go straight to the world

what: two editor tabs attached to one dev server both answer the bridge and first reply wins, so a state-dependent CLI test can read the other tab's world and fail intermittently
fix: have the bridge pick one client, or make the CLI say how many are attached

what: the repo had thirteen stale vite dev servers left running from earlier sessions, squatting ports 5180-5192, so a fresh npm run dev landed on an unpredictable port and the CLI default of 5180 pointed at a dead one
fix: a dev script that refuses to start when the port is taken, or an engine op that lists and kills stale servers

what: curl to localhost went through an HTTP proxy and returned 502 with an empty body, which read as the dev server being broken rather than as the request never arriving
fix: use --noproxy '*' when checking a local endpoint by hand; bin/engine.mjs uses node fetch and was never affected

what: check does not verify that a level's placements name types that exist — a level full of typos passes clean, and the only symptom is entities with no mesh and no collider that sit there silently. Building a 281-entity map, a mistyped type name is invisible.
fix: problemsIn() already has index.levels[*].types and index.types — one set difference away from reporting it

what: a placement's mesh replaces the type's rather than merging with it, so every one of 233 brushes repeats texture, tiling and tint to change only the box. The level file is 3,300 lines where 1,300 would do, and every read of it costs the difference.
fix: merge placement.mesh over type.mesh key by key, the way properties already merge

what: test.at(id, x, y) has no z, so arranging anything in a 3D level has to go through test.set(id, 'z', v) instead — and nothing says so.
fix: test.at(id, x, y, z) with z optional

what: assetURL treated any name containing a slash as project-relative, so a subfolder under assets/ was unreachable: counter-strike/wall.png resolved to /project/counter-strike/wall.png. All 231 texture references in de_dust2 were dead, check passed clean, and the only symptom was a brown viewport. The same rule was duplicated in audio.js, so sounds had it too.
fix: resolve under assets/ unless the path starts with a project folder; make audio.js and the renderer share one rule, and make check verify the file exists

what: loading a level copied its camera mode into the editor's view, so opening any first-person level put the editor inside a perspective camera standing in a wall. A completely black viewport with an empty error log — the exact failure AGENTS.md names as the worst one.
fix: the level's camera block is the GAME camera; the camera plugin already adopts it on play and restores on stop, so the kernel must not copy mode at load

what: two editor tabs on one dev server both answer the bridge and the first reply wins, so engine.mjs reported the OTHER tab's level and camera while I was looking at this one. Nothing said the answer came from somewhere else.
fix: have snapshot report which tab answered, or refuse when more than one is attached

note: assetURL now resolves under assets/ unless the path names a project folder; audio.js matches. de_dust2 renders with zero errors.
the kernel no longer copies camera mode at level load — the game camera plugin owns it, adopting on play and restoring on stop.
placement mesh now merges over the type's key by key, and a save writes only the keys that disagree.

what: A plugin cannot register a type that survives boot: startWorld calls loader.boot() and then loadTypes(), which begins with world.types.clear(). loadTypes is also called as a local closure at line 330 rather than through editor.loadTypes, so wrapping it does not help either. I had to re-assert the type on every level:loaded with world.retype, which works but is not discoverable.
fix: a 'types' contribution point, or loadTypes registering plugin types after the clear

what: makeRenderer never exposes the THREE.WebGLRenderer it wraps, so no plugin can set renderer.shadowMap.enabled. A light can be given castShadow and the scene can be marked castShadow/receiveShadow, and three will still draw no shadow at all, with nothing in the log. I had to warn by name instead of making it work.
fix: expose the WebGLRenderer, or add setShadows(on) beside setSun/setFog

what: A level-wide block that wants to set a per-entity mesh key (a lightmap) cannot do it without the next save writing that key onto every placement it touched: world.toLevel compares e.mesh against e._definition.mesh, so any runtime change to mesh reads as a placement override.
fix: a way to mark a field as applied-at-load so toLevel ignores it, the way _extraKeys marks the opposite

what: bus.emit does not await its listeners, and nothing in bus.js, AGENTS.md or ARCHITECTURE.md says so. World Look read the level's world block in an async level:loaded handler, so world.look answered with the defaults before the file had been read — confidently, with no way to tell. Game Camera had already been bitten and worked around it with a held promise; World Look had not, and the two sat next to each other in plugins/builtin looking equally correct.
fix: say it in bus.js, or have emit return the listener promises so a caller can await them — and a rule that a level:loaded handler must assign its read rather than be its read

what: the rule for where an asset name resolves to lives only in engine/ui.js as assetURL, which returns a browser URL and cannot be imported by node. To make check verify that a named asset exists I had to copy the rule into engine/project-index.mjs. Two copies of one rule that must agree exactly, with nothing enforcing it — and when they drift, check either swears a file is there that the renderer cannot fetch, or reports two hundred missing assets that are all on disk.
fix: move the path half of the rule into a tiny module both sides import, leaving assetURL as the browser's '/project/' + assetPath(name)

what: index.assets is keyed by basename, so an asset in a subfolder never matched the name that referenced it — counter-strike/concrete.png was filed as concrete.png and its usedBy stayed empty, which reads as 'nothing uses this, safe to delete' for every one of the ninety Counter-Strike assets. Two files with the same basename in different folders also silently overwrite each other in the index. Nothing reports either; I found it by reading the build loop while adding the asset check.
fix: key index.assets by its path from project/, or at minimum resolve usedBy through the same rule the engine fetches by — done for usedBy, the key itself is still the basename

what: check is whole-project only, so 'what does check say about de_dust2' has no verb. I wrote a throwaway node -e importing project-index.mjs and filtering problems by file to answer it, which is exactly the shell one-liner AGENTS.md tells you to turn into a test — and it cannot be one, because check is not a project test.
fix: check [file-or-level], or group the problems by file in the output so one level's share of them is readable at a glance

what: a test is handed the test object and never the context, so anything a plugin puts on context can only be tested if the plugin also exports a live handle for it. mouse-look exports mouseLook.input, camera exports runningCamera(), and I had to export canStand from physics-3d purely so a test could reach it — three plugins carrying an export that exists for no reason but testability, and a fourth agent will invent a fourth spelling of it.
fix: hand test.context to a test, the way every hook already gets it

note: check now validates both halves. problemsIn() reports every asset a type or a level names that is not a file on disk — resolved through the same rule engine/ui.js fetches by, deduped per reference with a count and the first placement that named it, behind a summary line so '4 missing assets, named 231 times' and 'one missing asset' read differently — and missingTypes() reports every placement naming a type with no file, plus placements with no type at all. Proved against the real de_dust2 with its four newest textures hidden: 4 missing assets, named 50 times, each with the entity index that first named it.

what: a test is handed `test` and never `context`, so there is no way to call a plugin-contributed verb (context.damage, context.weapons.fire) or to subscribe to the bus from a test. Two lanes in this run independently worked around it by exporting the live context from their plugin module and importing it back in the test — which works only because a plugin module is a singleton, and reads like a trick rather than like the intended path.
fix: add `test.context` (or `test.run(id, args)` and `test.on(event, fn)`) to makeT in plugins/builtin/tests.js

what: a test can be disabled with an early return (or by asserting nothing at all) and the runner reports it as PASSED, because runOne() computes ok as !error && checks.every(c => c.ok) and an empty checks array satisfies every(). project/tests/buy-menu.js carried 'if (1) return' above ~110 lines of assertions and sat on the board as a green tick for its whole life. A dead test is indistinguishable from a covering one, which is worse than no test because it reads as coverage.
fix: in runOne(), a test whose checks array contains no assertion should be recorded as empty rather than as passing — ok: false with error 'made no assertions', and the panel/summary should carry the assertion count per test so coverage is a number on the board rather than a tick

what: after a headless run, project/.engine/tests.json is left ZERO BYTES: runAll() calls save(context) without awaiting it and the CLI process exits before files.writeJSON lands. So 'node bin/engine.mjs --headless run tests.results' answers {passed:0,failed:0,tests:[]} and the editor's Tests panel shows nothing after a headless run. On top of that no verb ever prints a test's assertion COUNT — summary() is compact on success, so a passing test is a tick with no number behind it and there is no way to tell 51 assertions from 0. I had to write a throwaway node --input-type=module script that starts a world, runs tests.run, sleeps 1.2s to let the unawaited write finish, and re-reads the file, purely to count assertions.
fix: await save(context) in runAll before returning, and put a checks count in summary() — { id, ok, ms, assertions } — so coverage is a number on stdout and in the panel

what: AGENTS.md says to give each agent its own git worktree when several need to WRITE to project/, but the whole Counter-Strike lane (project/plugins/*, project/levels/de_dust2.json, project/types/terrorist.js, most of project/tests/*) is UNTRACKED, so a git worktree comes up empty of exactly the files two agents are fighting over — the advice cannot be followed. I found a second session rewriting project/tests/buy-menu.js and project/plugins/counter-strike-hud.js underneath me: a Read returned content that was stale two minutes later, one headless run failed with 'groundSpeed is not defined' from a half-written plugin, and .engine/tests.json was clobbered by the other run. Nothing reports this; I only noticed by comparing mtimes and listing processes.
fix: say plainly that a worktree only isolates TRACKED files, so untracked work must be committed before a fan-out — and give the CLI a lock or a stamp (an owner id in .engine/) so a second writer on the same project file is reported by name instead of discovered by mtime

what: start() is never hooked on an entity spawned after play began, so a behaviour attached to a respawned or mid-round-spawned body runs update() with an uninitialised bag — the symptom is NaN or a frozen thing, never an error
fix: hook start on entity:added while playing; until then bot-brain re-initialises itself lazily from update()

what: one headless invocation runs exactly one op, so 'simulate 60 then read a plugin command' is impossible — soak-testing bots meant writing a throwaway node script around startWorldInNode, which is the one thing tests are supposed to replace
fix: let ops chain: node bin/engine.mjs --headless simulate 60 --then run navigation.bots

what: a test is handed 'test' and never 'context', so nothing a plugin contributed — raycast, navigation, weapons, match — can be asked anything from a test. Every 3D test in this project works around it by importing the plugin module and rebuilding its state from world.entities
fix: expose test.run(commandId, args) — the command surface is already the read-and-drive API and it would need no new concepts

what: A viewport of 0x0 is silent. The editor's bottom dock is an auto grid row, so a tall Tests panel pushes .mid to zero and the game draws into nothing — renderer.resize() calls setSize(0,0) and updateCamera() with aspect 0 without a word, and engine.errors() stays empty. I lost the same way again in play focus: absolutely positioning .bar took it out of the grid, every later row shuffled up one, and the only symptom was a black screen.
fix: resize() reports once, by name, when the canvas measures zero — 'the viewport is 0x0, so nothing can draw'. That is the blank-viewport-with-an-empty-error-log case AGENTS.md calls the worst thing the engine can hand you.

what: No verb answers 'how big is the picture'. snapshot reports the camera but not the viewport, so working out why the game was not filling the screen took five throwaway 'eval getBoundingClientRect' calls against #app, .mid, #centre, #viewport and #gl.
fix: snapshot already carries camera; give it viewport too — width, height and whether the shell is focused. One call instead of five evals, and it works for anyone checking a HUD's size.

what: npm test writes into the project it is testing and does not clean up when it fails. Its hot-reload probe spawned _probe_42280_2 into project/levels/de_dust2.json, the step that removes it failed, and the placement stayed on disk — so 'check' started failing on a level file I never touched and I had to hand-repair another agent's file to get back to ok. Its stdout tests also fail on any project whose plugins log, because a plugin's console.log lands in the JSON the CLI is parsing.
fix: the probe places into a scratch level of its own and deletes it in a finally, never into whichever level happens to be open; and AGENTS.md should say npm test writes to project/ so it is not safe beside another agent.

what: Nothing in the engine can answer "what nodes does this GLB have". The character export contract — weaponMount at the right hand, a hands root called "hands", a c4 child called "led" — exists only as prose in a brief and in comments, so I wrote a throwaway node script to parse the GLB JSON chunks by hand, both to confirm the node names and to read the models' bounding boxes for the viewmodel placement. Every number in the placement table depended on that script.
fix: a verb: model.nodes <file> listing named nodes and per-node bounds, or the same carried on the asset entry in .engine/index.json so it is one read rather than a script

what: Nothing the renderer builds can be read back, so verifying a new renderer feature meant four rounds of bin/engine.mjs eval with hand-written scene-graph traversals against the one live editor tab — is the weapon really under weaponMount, did setting the same model twice rebuild the group, did clearing remove it. Headless cannot draw, so there was no other way to check engine code I had just written.
fix: a verb: render.tree <id> reporting what the renderer built for an entity — model file, named nodes, what is attached to each — which is one call instead of four evals and works for pose as well as attachments

what: A phase:'frame' system does not run at all in edit mode — engine/index.js paints with renderer.sync and renderer.draw and never calls the frame systems — but both AGENTS.md and ARCHITECTURE.md describe the frame as "systems with phase frame, then sync, then draw", one list, no caveat. I wrote a frame system with an "is the game running" guard that could never fire, and only found out by reading loop.js and index.js. The real consequence is that anything a frame system puts on screen has to be taken off by a play:stopped handler instead.
fix: one line in the 'One frame' section: in edit mode only sync and draw run, so a frame system cannot clean up after itself and must listen for play:stopped

what: The weapons lane emits weapon:reloaded when the magazine LANDS and emits nothing when a reload starts, so a lane told to animate a reload from the bus plays the whole motion after the ammunition counter has already gone up — the exact disagreement an animation timed to reloadSeconds exists to avoid. The only way to start the motion at the right moment is to read the carrying bag's reloadStartedAt and reloadingUntil directly, which is a second contract nothing announces. Found by reading weapons.js and carries-weapons.js after grepping for an event that turned out not to be emitted where it was described.
fix: emit weapon:reloading { entity, weapon, seconds } from reload() when the magazine change starts, so the bus carries both ends of it and nobody has to read another lane's timestamps

what: saveLevel wrote the editor's camera mode into the level, and the editor always opens in ortho so a first-person level could be silently demoted to a flat one by any save. Pressing play then gave the 2D camera and the level file looked correct at a glance because only one word had changed.
fix: never write mode from the editor: the camera block's mode is the game's rule, only at and zoom are the editor's

what: plugins.list returns only a name, so 'what does this plugin contribute' cannot be answered from the terminal — not its commands, not its contribution points, not whether it is builtin or the game's. Listing 36 plugins meant reading all 36 files off disk and regex-scraping them, which also picked the wrong name four times because the first name: in a file is not always the plugin's.
fix: have plugins.list report name, source (builtin or project), the contribution points it fills, its command ids, and what it assigns onto context — the loader already holds all of it

note: added Agent Workspace: focused instruction lanes, clean-baseline checks, atomic file claims, and automatic worktrees for parallel writers

what: The first step both front doors name does not work on a cold start. ENGINE-BASE.md says to get the packet first with agent.context <file>, but a fresh session told to understand this repo has no file yet. Bare agent.context answers with 346 characters of core rules and nothing else: no map, no shape of the codebase, no where to start. So the one documented step was skipped and orientation was hand-rolled from git diff --stat, head on a dozen files, and grep, which is exactly what the packet exists to replace. Onboarding is precisely when you do not yet know your file.
fix: agent.context with no arguments should answer the onboarding packet rather than the bare core rules: the shape of the repo, the front door, the checks that must pass, and the one command to run next. Or a named lane, agent.context --onboard.

what: Three front doors before any content. CLAUDE.md redirects to AGENTS.md, AGENTS.md (17 lines) redirects to ENGINE-BASE.md, ENGINE-BASE.md (34 lines) points at ARCHITECTURE.md, which is itself an index over six docs. AGENTS.md and ENGINE-BASE.md overlap almost completely: both say read this first, both list where everything lives, both name agent.context. Four reads and about 55 lines before the first sentence that describes what the engine is.
fix: Fold AGENTS.md into ENGINE-BASE.md and let AGENTS.md be the generated one-line pointer it already is for CLAUDE.md, so a cold reader lands on real content at the first hop.

what: ENGINE-BASE.md and AGENTS.md both say to read project/.engine/index.agent.json before opening many project files, but .engine/ is gitignored and the file is only written when the index is built. On a cold clone it is absent and nothing says so, so the instruction reads as though the file is always there. I read the generator in engine/project-index.mjs to learn what it would have held instead of reading the file.
fix: Say in the instruction that the index is generated, and name the command that writes it, so a reader whose clone has no .engine/ knows what to run rather than assuming the path is wrong.

what: Learning what a plugin does cold costs one head per file: seven times for the new plugins on this branch alone. p37 already asks for plugins.list to report more than a name, but it asks the loader, which needs a running editor. Onboarding happens with nothing running, so that fix would not have helped here. The .agent.md sidecars are already on disk and already carry a one-line purpose, and so does the header comment of every plugin file.
fix: A verb that reads the sidecars straight off disk, the way index and check already do: list every plugin with its name, its file and the first line of its guide, with no editor attached. It answers in a fresh clone, which is when it is needed most. Pairs with p37, which covers the live half.

what: docs/claude-orchestration/ is listed nowhere. The doc table in ARCHITECTURE.md names the six files in docs/ and that directory is not one of them, so the only way to meet it is to list the directory. I found it while staging a commit, not while reading the docs.
fix: Either add it to the ARCHITECTURE.md table or move it out of docs/, since it documents workspace tooling rather than the engine and a reader of the engine docs has no use for it.

what: A read-only headless run silently rewrote a level. Running "node bin/engine.mjs --headless run agents.list" — a command that only lists registered plugins and touches no entity — left project/levels/de_dust2.json modified on disk: one brush moved from [18,3,-6] to [22,4,-7]. Nothing was said, check still passed, and the change was found only by reading git status while committing something else. A verb that reads must not write. This is the same family as p31, but worse, because p31 was a test suite that at least announced it was running and this is an ordinary list command.
fix: A headless run should open the level read-only unless the op is one that writes. If the world must tick to answer at all, it must not save at shutdown — and if a save is ever right, the run should say which file it wrote, by name, on stderr.

note: Withdrawn — misattributed. The brush move was a person editing in the editor, not a headless run writing. No verb wrote anything it should not have; the timing looked like a headless save and I did not check with the author before filing.

what: The context packet for engine/shell.js still names npm test as a required check, but the project test suite was removed and the brief forbids running it — two instructions that disagree, and the agent has to pick
fix: Drop npm test from the tests list in agents/engine.md and agents/editor.md, or replace it with the node --test files that still run

what: Kernel logic that only runs in a browser has nowhere to be proven — I had to export the matcher and drive it from a throwaway script in agent-runs/, because test/ is not in my lane and no headless harness renders a shell
fix: A test/shell.*.test.mjs that imports the pure parts of the kernel, so a DOM-shaped change is provable by node --test instead of by a script that gets deleted

what: Three plugins each carried the same copied asset rule under the same comment: Written out here rather than imported because a plugin receives `ui`, it does not import it. That sentence is false, and it was the whole reason p18's two copies had quietly become five. plugins/builtin/skybox.js and materials.js already import assetURL from ../../engine/ui.js, and agent-workspace.js imports from engine/ at the top of the file. Disproving one sentence that appears verbatim in three files cost a grep of the repo plus reads of engine/index.js and start-world-node.mjs to confirm a builtin plugin really is an ES module on both sides. Nothing in the engine could have caught it: a false reason for a copy reads exactly like a true one.
fix: Plugin Master says how a plugin composes UI but never says whether a plugin may import an engine module, and three files filled the silence with the wrong answer. One line: a builtin plugin may import from engine/, and must, rather than restating a kernel rule in its own words.

what: The instruction packet for engine/** names `npm test` as a required check, and p31 already records that npm test writes into project/ and is not safe beside another agent. My lane brief forbade running it for exactly that reason. So the one command the packet tells me to run before finishing is the one command I am told not to run, and nothing in the packet says which to obey. I reconciled it by hand and ran the two node --test files instead, which are safe and needed nothing running.
fix:
Name the safe checks in the packet and mark the unsafe one: 
ode bin/engine.mjs check and 
ode --test test/cli.offline.test.mjs test/agent-workspace.test.mjs always, 
pm test only with a dev server, an open tab and exclusive use of project/.

what: The pain verb silently corrupts any fix text that quotes a command. On PowerShell a backtick is the escape character, so passing --fix run `npm test` only with a dev server stored run \npm test only with a dev server — the backticks were eaten and a backslash left behind. It landed in p47 and there is no way to correct it: the only verbs are pain, pain.list and pain.resolve, so a filed record is immutable and a mangled one stays mangled forever. A friction log whose entries cannot be edited has to be right first time, and nothing warns that the shell got there first.
fix: Two things. Say in help that a pain naming a command should be passed with a here-string, since every fix worth reading names a command and PowerShell is the shell on this machine. And add pain.amend <id> --fix ... so a record filed with a mangled or wrong field can be corrected without resolving it falsely or filing a duplicate.

note: Took the fix this record suggested. engine/asset-path.js now holds the path half alone — a pure function, no URL prefix, no DOM, no node import — and its header says the opposite of project-index.mjs: both halves may import this one. assetURL in engine/ui.js is now /project/ + assetPath(source) and is the only place that knows the prefix. There were five copies, not two: project-index.mjs imports it instead of its hand-copy, and audio.js, decals.js and particles.js import assetURL from engine/ui.js instead of restating the rule under a comment claiming a plugin cannot import. All five agreed before the change, so nothing had to be chosen between. check reports {ok:true,problems:[]} before and after, and agent-runs/asset-path-agreement.mjs checks 13 names — including counter-strike/wall.png and names that start with a project folder — against the rule as engine/ui.js:35 carried it, so behaviour did not change is a run rather than a claim.

what: No chokepoint for an edit. The Inspector writes entity[key]=value onto the live entity and the Transform Tool mutates inside pointermove, so a history plugin cannot record a command or a diff and has to snapshot the whole level on every change.
fix: One verb every editor edit goes through — context.edit(entity, changes) — that applies the change, announces it with the before and after, and saves.

what: A drag and an arrow nudge announce nothing at all. The Transform Tool mutates the entity and calls context.save(), never emitting world:changed, so the single most common edit is invisible to any listener and History had to also subscribe to files:written for the open level.
fix: Emit world:changed alongside context.save() in tool-transform's end() and arrow-key branch, or have saveLevel announce the save on the bus as an edit.

what: writeAtomic names its temp file by process id alone, so two overlapping buildIndex calls in ONE process both write index.json.<pid>.tmp and the second rename throws ENOENT. Reachable in normal use: context.save() is fire-and-forget and arrow-key auto-repeat fires many of them.
fix: Add a per-call counter to the temp name (index.json.<pid>.<n>.tmp), the way importFresh already counts its cache-busting query.

what: The editor has no clock. context.time only advances while the loop runs and every wall clock is banned, so a plugin cannot coalesce a burst of edits by time. History had to infer a gesture from what changed instead, which merges two separate drags of the same entity into one entry.
fix: Announce a gesture: an edit:begin / edit:end pair from tools that drag, or an editor-side tick that advances outside play.

what: Every kernel emit of world:changed passes no payload, so a listener is told that something changed and never what. Any plugin that cares has to re-serialise the whole world and diff it against its own copy.
fix: Pass what moved: bus.emit('world:changed', { entities: [id], reason }) at each of the five kernel emit sites.

what: p25 was resolved by building the Agent Workspace, but only the coordination half of it. File claims are still advisory: no write path reads project/.engine/agents.json. engine/files.js write, the /api/file POST in vite.config.js, and the headless writer in engine/start-world-node.mjs all write unconditionally, so an agent that never calls agent.prepare is invisible to the registry and a claimed file is not actually protected. This is exactly the failure p25 described — a second session rewriting files underneath the first, found by comparing mtimes — and the registry that was built to answer it does not answer it. Worse for game work: saveLevel rewrites the whole level file, so two agents editing one level lose a write rather than getting a conflict.
fix: Check the active claims inside the one writer every path already goes through. A write to a file another run has claimed should be refused by name — which run holds it, and since when — rather than silently winning. Same check in the /api/file POST and the headless writer, or two of the three doors stay open.

what: There is no way to finish a parallel run. agent.release only flips a status in the registry: the git worktree and the agent/<id> branch both survive, so N lanes means N manual git merge, git worktree remove and git branch -d, done by hand by whoever is orchestrating. Re-preparing the same id later then fails at git worktree add because the branch still exists. test/agent-workspace.test.mjs proves this by having to remove both by hand. The cost is not the typing — it is that nothing detects a conflict between two lanes, so the orchestrator maintains a disjoint-file list in its head and finds out it was wrong at merge time.
fix: An agent.merge <id> verb that merges the lane branch, reports conflicts by name rather than failing silently, removes the worktree and deletes the branch. Also settle whether a worktree needs its own npm install: worktrees resolve three and vite today only because .agent-worktrees/ is nested inside the main checkout and node walks up, and nobody has tested moving them.

what: agent.release --checked records nothing real. releaseAgent copies the lane list of required tests into the record on the caller say-so; no check is executed and no result is read. So "completion is refused until every lane-required check is recorded", which docs/agent-workspace.md states as a guarantee, is an honour system — an agent that never ran a test releases exactly as cleanly as one that did. It is worse than no gate, because the registry then carries a record that reads as proof. Compounding it: the required list for the engine, editor and tooling lanes is npm test, and test/cli.test.mjs needs a running dev server and one open editor tab, so N parallel agents cannot all satisfy it even in principle.
fix: Run the checks, or stop claiming they were run. Either execute each lane-required command and record its exit code and output, or rename the flag to say what it means. Also mark which checks are safe in parallel — npm test writes into project/ and needs the one shared editor tab, so it belongs to a serial step in main at the end, not to a lane.

what: Vite's define is silently inert in dev for a bare identifier — vite:define returns immediately when command is serve and not ssr, so ENGINE_PROJECT_DIRECTORY was replaced in a production build and never in the editor. The parameter looked correct in the source and quietly reverted to 'project' in the only thing anyone runs. Only keys starting with import.meta.env. survive dev, injected by vite:import-analysis.
fix: Say in docs/kernel.md that import.meta.env is the ONLY channel that hands a build-time value to the browser half in dev, and that a bare define works in build only.

what: Nothing carries the project directory into context, so a plugin cannot say which project a headless world opened. startWorldInNode knows it, startWorld never hears it, and editor only gets game.json's title. Project Switcher has to answer 'screen: false' headless rather than name the directory, and assetURL in node still assumes 'project'.
fix: Set editor.projectDirectory from the caller in startWorld, the way editor.projectName is set from game.json.

what: loadPlugins is called with no arguments, so the browser half had to construct a second overHTTP() transport just to list project plugins from files.tree(). The one that startWorld already built from openFiles is unreachable from there.
fix: Call loadPlugins(files) — the files object exists three lines earlier and every other hook already receives context.

what: engine/ui.js line 18 re-exports assetURL with 'export { assetURL } from ./asset-path.js', which creates no local binding, but lines 248 and 262 call assetURL(src) as if it did. ui.thumb and ui.preview therefore throw ReferenceError for any image source. Nothing in the Counter-Strike editor's default view reaches them, so it is silent until a panel shows a thumbnail and is then disabled by the shell's catch.
fix: Import assetURL as well as re-exporting it: import { assetURL } from './asset-path.js' plus export { assetURL }.

note: Imported as well as re-exported in engine/ui.js. 'export { x } from' forwards a name without creating a local binding, so ui.thumb and ui.preview called an assetURL that was not in scope. My own defect, from the asset-path collapse.

Recorded in docs/kernel.md beside the browser-and-node split: import.meta.env is the only define channel that survives dev, because Vite's define plugin returns early when not building. The project directory travels that way.

what: The engine plugins are AI-facing but sized for a human reader. 19 of 47 are over 400 lines and five are over 900 — weapons.js 1194, counter-strike-hud.js 1006, particles.js 1003, match-rules.js 946, buy-menu.js 891. Using one is cheap, because every plugin has a sidecar guide and the guides are around ten lines. Editing one is not: finding the part to change in a thousand-line file costs more context than the change. World Look was split into Skybox, View 3D and Gizmo 3D for exactly this reason and each is readable alone; nothing else has had the same treatment.
fix: Split by what a file owns, not by length, when you are already in it for another reason. plugin.sizes names every one that is over. The four worst builtins are particles, lights, materials and physics-3d; the project plugins are worse but are the game, not the engine.

note: Claim Guard, a plugin, refuses a write to a file another active run claimed. The kernel got a narrow files.guardWrites hook so the policy stays in a plugin that can be switched off; the guard reads the registry and names the run that holds the file. Also fixed the boot order that made switching it off meaningless.
agent.merge lands the lane, runs its deferred checks in the main worktree, removes the worktree and deletes the branch, so an id is reusable.

agent.release runs each required check in the lane workspace, records command, exit code and output, and refuses to complete when one fails. Checks needing the one dev server are deferred by name and run by agent.merge.

what: Nothing told a game-building agent where a new capability belongs, so capability got written inside the game and had to be found and rebranded by hand afterwards. The Counter-Strike gauntlet produced project plugins that are generic engine work wearing one game name — damage, radar, bot-navigation, weapon models — and separating them was manual. Worse, docs/design.md lists "triggers separate from solids" as a KNOWN ENGINE GAP, so an agent needing a 2D trigger today reads that as missing and writes it as game code, and the gap stays open while the capability exists inside one project.
fix: Plugin Master now carries a "which folder" rule: capability is the engine, rules are the game; would a second game want this and would you have to rename it first. plugin.sizes reports a builtin whose code mentions the game title. Still open: the eight Counter-Strike project plugins that are really engine capability have not been promoted.

note: writeAtomic takes a per-call counter as well as the pid, so two overlapping buildIndex calls in one process no longer share a temporary name. Fixed in 5cbaa20 alongside History.

Plugin Master now carries the which-folder rule: capability is the engine, rules are the game, and the test is whether a second game would want it and would have to rename it first. plugin.sizes reports a builtin whose code names the game. The Counter-Strike project plugins stay branded and stay where they are — a project plugin is SUPPOSED to speak its game's language, and promoting one that only sounds generic costs more than it returns.

runOne counts assertions and refuses to pass a test that made none. note() does not count. The summary and each passing test now carry an assertion count, so coverage is a number rather than a tick. Proved by agent-runs/2026-08-30-parallel/empty-test.mjs.

The lane checks are split: npm run test:offline is the two suites that need nothing running, and lanes run it. npm test still chains the bridge suite that writes into project/ and needs one editor tab, so it is deferred and agent.merge runs it once in the main worktree.
Same split. The engine, editor and tooling packets name npm run test:offline as the check a lane runs, and npm test as the serial one agent.merge runs after the lane lands.

A test is handed test.context — the same object every hook gets. The three module-level handles that existed only so a test could import them back are gone: camera's runningCamera (context.camera was always the same object), mouse-look's mouseLook.input (it is context.input), and physics-3d's exported canStand (it was already context.canStand). Proof: agent-runs/2026-08-30-parallel/test-context.mjs.

makeT now gives a test three ways into the engine: test.context (the live context), test.run(id, args) (drive a command the way the terminal does) and test.on(event, handler) (the bus, unsubscribed for you when the test ends, so a handler cannot leak into the next test). No plugin module import needed.

test.run(commandId, args) exists — the command surface was already the read-and-drive API, so it needed no new concepts. test.context reaches anything a plugin contributed directly. Rebuilding plugin state from world.entities is no longer the only path.

what: agent.prepare refuses any claim that overlaps another lane's directory claim, so one agent claiming kitten-survivors/plugins locks every other lane out of the whole project plugin folder even for brand-new files nobody else will touch
fix: Overlap should be per-file, not prefix: a directory claim should only block files that already exist in it, or agent.prepare should offer --except / allow disjoint new-file claims inside a claimed directory
